paper_metadata.title: AI-Assisted Pipeline for Dynamic Generation of Trustworthy Health Supplement Content at Scale
paper_metadata.venue: DROPS (Schloss Dagstuhl – Leibniz Center for Informatics)
paper_metadata.abstract: Although geospatial question answering systems have received increasing attention in recent years, existing prototype systems struggle to properly answer qualitative spatial questions. In this work, we propose a unique framework for answering qualitative spatial questions, which comprises three main components: a geoparser that takes the input questions and extracts place semantic information from text, a reasoning system which is embedded with a crisp reasoner, and finally, answer extraction, which refines the solution space and generates final answers. We present an experimental design to evaluate our framework for point-based cardinal direction calculus (CDC) relations by developing an automated approach for generating three types of synthetic qualitative spatial questions. The initial evaluations of generated answers in our system are promising because a high proportion of answers were labelled correct.

paper_metadata.title: ChatGPT for good? On opportunities and challenges of large language models for education
A Systematic Study and Comprehensive Evaluation of ChatGPT on Benchmark Datasets
paper_metadata.abstract: The development of large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT has brought a lot of attention recently. However, their evaluation in the benchmark academic datasets remains under-explored due to the difficulty of evaluating the generative outputs produced by this model against the ground truth. In this paper, we aim to present a thorough evaluation of ChatGPT's performance on diverse academic datasets, covering tasks like question-answering, text summarization, code generation, commonsense reasoning, mathematical problem-solving, machine translation, bias detection, and ethical considerations. Specifically, we evaluate ChatGPT across 140 tasks and analyze 255K responses it generates in these datasets. This makes our work the largest evaluation of ChatGPT in NLP benchmarks. In short, our study aims to validate the strengths and weaknesses of ChatGPT in various tasks and provide insights for future research using LLMs. We also report a new emergent ability to follow multi-query instructions that we mostly found in ChatGPT and other instruction-tuned models. Our extensive evaluation shows that even though ChatGPT is capable of performing a wide variety of tasks, and may obtain impressive performance in several benchmark datasets, it is still far from achieving the ability to reliably solve many challenging tasks. By providing a thorough assessment of ChatGPT's performance across diverse NLP tasks, this paper sets the stage for a targeted deployment of ChatGPT-like LLMs in real-world applications.

paper_metadata.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for AI-Generated Content: A Survey
paper_metadata.abstract: Advancements in model algorithms, the growth of foundational models, and access to high-quality datasets have propelled the evolution of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC). Despite its notable successes, AIGC still faces hurdles such as updating knowledge, handling long-tail data, mitigating data leakage, and managing high training and inference costs. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has recently emerged as a paradigm to address such challenges. In particular, RAG introduces the information retrieval process, which enhances the generation process by retrieving relevant objects from available data stores, leading to higher accuracy and better robustness. In this paper, we comprehensively review existing efforts that integrate RAG technique into AIGC scenarios. We first classify RAG foundations according to how the retriever augments the generator, distilling the fundamental abstractions of the augmentation methodologies for various retrievers and generators. This unified perspective encompasses all RAG scenarios, illuminating advancements and pivotal technologies that help with potential future progress. We also summarize additional enhancements methods for RAG, facilitating effective engineering and implementation of RAG systems. Then from another view, we survey on practical applications of RAG across different modalities and tasks, offering valuable references for researchers and practitioners. Furthermore, we introduce the benchmarks for RAG, discuss the limitations of current RAG systems, and suggest potential directions for future research. Github: https://github.com/PKU-DAIR/RAG-Survey.

paper_metadata.title: Unsupervised Learning by Probabilistic Latent Semantic Analysis
Gradient-based learning applied to document recognition
paper_metadata.abstract: Multilayer neural networks trained with the back-propagation algorithm constitute the best example of a successful gradient based learning technique. Given an appropriate network architecture, gradient-based learning algorithms can be used to synthesize a complex decision surface that can classify high-dimensional patterns, such as handwritten characters, with minimal preprocessing. This paper reviews various methods applied to handwritten character recognition and compares them on a standard handwritten digit recognition task. Convolutional neural networks, which are specifically designed to deal with the variability of 2D shapes, are shown to outperform all other techniques. Real-life document recognition systems are composed of multiple modules including field extraction, segmentation recognition, and language modeling. A new learning paradigm, called graph transformer networks (GTN), allows such multimodule systems to be trained globally using gradient-based methods so as to minimize an overall performance measure. Two systems for online handwriting recognition are described. Experiments demonstrate the advantage of global training, and the flexibility of graph transformer networks. A graph transformer network for reading a bank cheque is also described. It uses convolutional neural network character recognizers combined with global training techniques to provide record accuracy on business and personal cheques. It is deployed commercially and reads several million cheques per day.

paper_metadata.title: Semantic memory: A review of methods, models, and current challenges
Why is constrained neural language generation particularly challenging?
paper_metadata.abstract: Recent advances in deep neural language models combined with the capacity of large scale datasets have accelerated the development of natural language generation systems that produce fluent and coherent texts (to various degrees of success) in a multitude of tasks and application contexts. However, controlling the output of these models for desired user and task needs is still an open challenge. This is crucial not only to customizing the content and style of the generated language, but also to their safe and reliable deployment in the real world. We present an extensive survey on the emerging topic of constrained neural language generation in which we formally define and categorize the problems of natural language generation by distinguishing between conditions and constraints (the latter being testable conditions on the output text instead of the input), present constrained text generation tasks, and review existing methods and evaluation metrics for constrained text generation. Our aim is to highlight recent progress and trends in this emerging field, informing on the most promising directions and limitations towards advancing the state-of-the-art of constrained neural language generation research.

paper_metadata.title: TEAL: Tokenize and Embed ALL for Multi-modal Large Language Models
paper_metadata.abstract: Despite Multi-modal Large Language Models (MM-LLMs) have made exciting strides recently, they are still struggling to efficiently model the interactions among multi-modal inputs and the generation in non-textual modalities. In this work, we propose TEAL (Tokenize and Embed ALl)}, an approach to treat the input from any modality as a token sequence and learn a joint embedding space for all modalities. Specifically, for the input from any modality, TEAL first discretizes it into a token sequence with the off-the-shelf tokenizer and embeds the token sequence into a joint embedding space with a learnable embedding matrix. MM-LLMs just need to predict the multi-modal tokens autoregressively as the textual LLMs do. Finally, the corresponding de-tokenizer is applied to generate the output in each modality based on the predicted token sequence. With the joint embedding space, TEAL enables the frozen LLMs to perform both understanding and generation tasks involving non-textual modalities, such as image and audio. Thus, the textual LLM can just work as an interface and maintain its high performance in textual understanding and generation. Experiments show that TEAL achieves substantial improvements in multi-modal understanding, and implements a simple scheme for multi-modal generations.

paper_metadata.title: A Multilevel Monte Carlo Asymptotic-Preserving Particle Method for Kinetic Equations in the Diffusion Limit
paper_metadata.abstract: We propose a multilevel Monte Carlo method for a particle-based asymptotic-preserving scheme for kinetic equations. Kinetic equations model transport and collision of particles in a position-velocity phase-space. With a diffusive scaling, the kinetic equation converges to an advection-diffusion equation in the limit of zero mean free path. Classical particle-based techniques suffer from a strict time-step restriction to maintain stability in this limit. Asymptotic-preserving schemes provide a solution to this time step restriction, but introduce a first-order error in the time step size. We demonstrate how the multilevel Monte Carlo method can be used as a bias reduction technique to perform accurate simulations in the diffusive regime, while leveraging the reduced simulation cost given by the asymptotic-preserving scheme. We describe how to achieve the necessary correlation between simulation paths at different levels and demonstrate the potential of the approach via numerical experiments.

rag_package.related_work_summary: Generating text that adheres to specific syntactic or semantic constraints is a critical challenge in large language model (LLM) applications, as highlighted by prior work surveying the difficulties in constrained neural language generation (Garbacea and Mei, 2022). While recent advancements have enabled impressive generative capabilities in LLMs like ChatGPT, their performance on diverse academic datasets still varies, especially concerning challenging tasks and reliable output (Laskar et al., 2023). Other approaches, such as tokenizing and embedding across modalities (Yang et al., 2023), address aspects of controlled generation by structuring inputs and outputs. Broader methodologies for enhancing LLM reliability include Retrieval-Augmented Generation to mitigate knowledge limitations (Zhao et al., 2024) and foundational probabilistic methods like Probabilistic Latent Semantic Analysis (Hofmann, 2001) that offer a probabilistic perspective on information extraction. The need for control extends to ensuring trustworthiness in generated content (Kefallinos et al., 2018; Kasneci et al., 2023). Our work directly addresses these challenges by developing an architecture for controlled LLM generation based on sequential Monte Carlo (SMC), offering a flexible and efficient way to incorporate inference-time constraints and providing a better approximation to the posterior distribution, distinguishing our approach from these existing paradigms.

strengths: The core idea of leveraging Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) for controlled Large Language Model (LLM) generation, particularly in integrating diverse and expensive constraints incrementally, is highly novel and innovative. The empirical evaluation across four challenging and diverse domains (Python code generation, text-to-SQL, goal inference, and molecule synthesis) strongly demonstrates the versatility and effectiveness of the proposed SMC framework. The results show significant performance improvements, often allowing smaller LMs to outperform much larger or fine-tuned models.

weaknesses: While the paper generally highlights the benefits of SMC, a more detailed discussion or ablation of the specific 'cheap stochastic approximations' mentioned in the 'Further extensions' section (Appendix C) would be beneficial, as these seem to play a role in making otherwise 'modestly expensive' Φeff tractable. reviewers.summary_comment: This paper presents a truly exciting and novel approach to controlled language model generation using Sequential Monte Carlo. The focus on programmable potentials and the rigorous validation of the probabilistic perspective further strengthen the work. Minor methodological details could be refined, but the core innovation and its demonstrated impact make this a highly significant contribution that promises to inspire new research directions in controlled generation. This is precisely the kind of bold, forward-looking research that merits acceptance.

strengths: The paper provides a methodologically sound and rigorous application of Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) to controlled text generation. This rigorous evaluation goes beyond mere accuracy metrics to explain *why* the method works.
weaknesses: While the concept of "programmable potentials and proposals" is introduced, the paper could provide more details or concrete examples beyond the general descriptions (e.g., integrating libraries, waiting for full lines of code). The computational overhead discussion mentions that the cost of expensive potentials "rarely rises above ~30ms per token" and that they are often performed on CPU. This environment should further support the practical implementation and application of embodied agents. However, the environments and tasks for embodied intelligence the existing research mainly focuses on are relatively limited (Duan et al., 2022). Many works (Shridhar et al., 2020; Deitke et al., 2022; Gao et al., 2021) only consider the indoor scenarios for embodied intelligence. These tasks include visual QA tasks targeting certain objects or simple task decomposition in the room (Azuma et al.,
2022; Francis et al., 2022). Such benchmarks actually restrict the validation of embodied agents' capabilities within a very narrow boundary, with low task difficulty and a large gap to artificial general intelligence. Therefore, in this paper, we consider extending embodied agents from indoor rooms to outdoor cities, expanding tasks beyond the indoor spaces to a broader urban environment. There are a few works that build a 3D urban environment for EmbodiedAI such as MetaUrban (Wu et al., 2024), GRUtopia (Wang et al., 2024), and AerialVLN (Liu et al., 2023), but they are limited in either the environment or the benchmark (**we analyze the limitations in detail from 9 dimensions** in Table 1). Specifically, all of these works consider a fictional city. Either they employ a highly simplified environment or only set up one or two embodied tasks. There are also some other efforts that use street view images to construct the environment, which significantly limits the potential Embodied AI tasks. In this commercial district, we establish realistic and detailed citybuilding 3D models as the foundation for the entire benchmark platform. paper_metadata.title: Real-World Robot Applications of Foundation Models: A Review
paper_metadata.abstract: Recent developments in foundation models, like Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs), trained on extensive data, facilitate flexible application across different tasks and modalities. Their impact spans various fields, including healthcare, education, and robotics. This paper provides an overview of the practical application of foundation models in real-world robotics, with a primary emphasis on the replacement of specific components within existing robot systems. The summary encompasses the perspective of input-output relationships in foundation models, as well as their role in perception, motion planning, and control within the field of robotics. This paper concludes with a discussion of future challenges and implications for practical robot applications.

paper_metadata.title: Contributions and Risks of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Building Smarter Cities: Insights from a Systematic Review of the Literature
paper_metadata.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is one of the most disruptive technologies of our time. Interest in the use of AI for urban innovation continues to grow. Particularly, the rise of smart cities—urban locations that are enabled by community, technology, and policy to deliver productivity, innovation, livability, wellbeing, sustainability, accessibility, good governance, and good planning—has increased the demand for AI-enabled innovations. There is, nevertheless, no scholarly work that provides a comprehensive review on the topic. This paper generates insights into how AI can contribute to the development of smarter cities. A systematic review of the literature is selected as the methodologic approach. Results are categorized under the main smart city development dimensions, i.e., economy, society, environment, and governance. The findings of the systematic review containing 93 articles disclose that: (a) AI in the context of smart cities is an emerging field of research and practice. (b) The central focus of the literature is on AI technologies, algorithms, and their current and prospective applications. (c) AI applications in the context of smart cities mainly concentrate on business efficiency, data analytics, education, energy, environmental sustainability, health, land use, security, transport, and urban management areas. (d) There is limited scholarly research investigating the risks of wider AI utilization. (e) Upcoming disruptions of AI in cities and societies have not been adequately examined. Current and potential contributions of AI to the development of smarter cities are outlined in this paper to inform scholars of prospective areas for further research.

paper_metadata.title: AI-big data analytics for building automation and management systems: a survey, actual challenges and future perspectives
paper_metadata.abstract: In theory, building automation and management systems (BAMSs) can provide all the components and functionalities required for analyzing and operating buildings. However, in reality, these systems can only ensure the control of heating ventilation and air conditioning system systems. Therefore, many other tasks are left to the operator, e.g. evaluating buildings' performance, detecting abnormal energy consumption, identifying the changes needed to improve efficiency, ensuring the security and privacy of end-users, etc. To that end, there has been a movement for developing artificial intelligence (AI) big data analytic tools as they offer various new and tailor-made solutions that are incredibly appropriate for practical buildings' management. Typically, they can help the operator in (i) analyzing the tons of connected equipment data; and; (ii) making intelligent, efficient, and on-time decisions to improve the buildings' performance. This paper presents a comprehensive systematic survey on using AI-big data analytics in BAMSs. It covers various AI-based tasks, e.g. load forecasting, water management, indoor environmental quality monitoring, occupancy detection, etc. The first part of this paper adopts a well-designed taxonomy to overview existing frameworks. A comprehensive review is conducted about different aspects, including the learning process, building environment, computing platforms, and application scenario. Moving on, a critical discussion is performed to identify current challenges. The second part aims at providing the reader with insights into the real-world application of AI-big data analytics. Thus, three case studies that demonstrate the use of AI-big data analytics in BAMSs are presented, focusing on energy anomaly detection in residential and office buildings and energy and performance optimization in sports facilities. Lastly, future directions and valuable recommendations are identified to improve the performance and reliability of BAMSs in intelligent buildings.

paper_metadata.title: Spatial models for context-aware indoor navigation systems: A survey
paper_metadata.abstract: This paper surveys indoor spatial models developed for research fields ranging from mobile robot mapping, to indoor location-based services (LBS), and most recently to context-aware navigation services applied to indoor environments. Over the past few years, several studies have evaluated the potential of spatial models for robot navigation and ubiquitous computing. In this paper we take a slightly different perspective, considering not only the underlying properties of those spatial models, but also to which degree the notion of context can be taken into account when delivering services in indoor environments. Some preliminary recommendations for the development of indoor spatial models are introduced from a context-aware perspective. A taxonomy of models is then presented and assessed with the aim of providing a flexible spatial data model for navigation purposes, and by taking into account the context dimensions.

paper_metadata.title: Gibson Env: Real-World Perception for Embodied Agents
paper_metadata.abstract: Developing visual perception models for active agents and sensorimotor control are cumbersome to be done in the physical world, as existing algorithms are too slow to efficiently learn in real-time and robots are fragile and costly. This has given rise to learning-in-simulation which consequently casts a question on whether the results transfer to real-world. In this paper, we are concerned with the problem of developing real-world perception for active agents, propose Gibson Virtual Environment for this purpose, and showcase sample perceptual tasks learned therein. Gibson is based on virtualizing real spaces, rather than using artificially designed ones, and currently includes over 1400 floor spaces from 572 full buildings. The main characteristics of Gibson are: I. being from the real-world and reflecting its semantic complexity, II. having an internal synthesis mechanism, "Goggles", enabling deploying the trained models in real-world without needing further domain adaptation, III. embodiment of agents and making them subject to constraints of physics and space.

paper_metadata.title: Vision-and-Language Navigation: A Survey of Tasks, Methods, and Future Directions
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the 60th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
paper_metadata.abstract: A long-term goal of AI research is to build intelligent agents that can communicate with humans in natural language, perceive the environment, and perform real-world tasks. Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) is a fundamental and interdisciplinary research topic towards this goal, and receives increasing attention from natural language processing, computer vision, robotics, and machine learning communities. In this paper, we review contemporary studies in the emerging field of VLN, covering tasks, evaluation metrics, methods, etc. Through structured analysis of current progress and challenges, we highlight the limitations of current VLN and opportunities for future work. This paper serves as a thorough reference for the VLN research community.

paper_metadata.title: EmbodiedCity: A Benchmark Platform for Embodied Agent in Real-world City Environment
paper_metadata.abstract: Embodied artificial intelligence emphasizes the role of an agent's body in generating human-like behaviors. The recent efforts on EmbodiedAI pay a lot of attention to building up machine learning models to possess perceiving, planning, and acting abilities, thereby enabling real-time interaction with the world. However, most works focus on bounded indoor environments, such as navigation in a room or manipulating a device, with limited exploration of embodying the agents in open-world scenarios. That is, embodied intelligence in the open and outdoor environment is less explored, for which one potential reason is the lack of high-quality simulators, benchmarks, and datasets. To address it, in this paper, we construct a benchmark platform for embodied intelligence evaluation in real-world city environments. Specifically, we first construct a highly realistic 3D simulation environment based on the real buildings, roads, and other elements in a real city. In this environment, we combine historically collected data and simulation algorithms to conduct simulations of pedestrian and vehicle flows with high fidelity. Further, we designed a set of evaluation tasks covering different EmbodiedAI abilities. Moreover, we provide a complete set of input and output interfaces for access, enabling embodied agents to easily take task requirements and current environmental observations as input and then make decisions and obtain performance evaluations. On the one hand, it expands the capability of existing embodied intelligence to higher levels. On the other hand, it has a higher practical value in the real world and can support more potential applications for artificial general intelligence. Based on this platform, we evaluate some popular large language models for embodied intelligence capabilities of different dimensions and difficulties.

paper_metadata.title: Soft actuators for real-world applications
paper_metadata.abstract: Inspired by physically adaptive, agile, reconfigurable and multifunctional soft-bodied animals and human muscles, soft actuators have been developed for a variety of applications, including soft grippers, artificial muscles, wearables, haptic devices and medical devices. However, the complex performance of biological systems cannot yet be fully replicated in synthetic designs. In this Review, we discuss new materials and structural designs for the engineering of soft actuators with physical intelligence and advanced properties, such as adaptability, multimodal locomotion, self-healing and multi-responsiveness. We examine how performance can be improved and multifunctionality implemented by using programmable soft materials, and highlight important real-world applications of soft actuators. Finally, we discuss the challenges and opportunities for next-generation soft actuators, including physical intelligence, adaptability, manufacturing scalability and reproducibility, extended lifetime and end-of-life strategies. Soft actuators are flexible and compliant and thus perfectly suited to interact with the human body. This Review discusses tethered, untethered and biohybrid soft actuation strategies, highlights promising real-world applications of soft robots and identifies key future challenges, such as implementing physical intelligence and end-of-life strategies.

paper_metadata.title: Urban Mobility
paper_metadata.abstract: In this chapter, we discuss urban mobility from a complexity science perspective. First, we give an overview of the datasets that enable this approach, such as mobile phone records, location-based social network traces, or GPS trajectories from sensors installed on vehicles. We then review the empirical and theoretical understanding of the properties of human movements, including the distribution of travel distances and times, the entropy of trajectories, and the interplay between exploration and exploitation of locations. Next, we explain generative and predictive models of individual mobility, and their limitations due to intrinsic limits of predictability. Finally, we discuss urban transport from a systemic perspective, including system-wide challenges like ridesharing, multimodality, and sustainable transport.

paper_metadata.title: MetaUrban: An Embodied AI Simulation Platform for Urban Micromobility
paper_metadata.abstract: Public urban spaces like streetscapes and plazas serve residents and accommodate social life in all its vibrant variations. Recent advances in Robotics and Embodied AI make public urban spaces no longer exclusive to humans. Food delivery bots and electric wheelchairs have started sharing sidewalks with pedestrians, while robot dogs and humanoids have recently emerged in the street. Micromobility enabled by AI for short-distance travel in public urban spaces plays a crucial component in the future transportation system. Ensuring the generalizability and safety of AI models maneuvering mobile machines is essential. In this work, we present MetaUrban, a compositional simulation platform for the AI-driven urban micromobility research. MetaUrban can construct an infinite number of interactive urban scenes from compositional elements, covering a vast array of ground plans, object placements, pedestrians, vulnerable road users, and other mobile agents' appearances and dynamics. We design point navigation and social navigation tasks as the pilot study using MetaUrban for urban micromobility research and establish various baselines of Reinforcement Learning and Imitation Learning. We conduct extensive evaluation across mobile machines, demonstrating that heterogeneous mechanical structures significantly influence the learning and execution of AI policies. We perform a thorough ablation study, showing that the compositional nature of the simulated environments can substantially improve the generalizability and safety of the trained mobile agents. MetaUrban will be made publicly available to provide research opportunities and foster safe and trustworthy embodied AI and micromobility in cities. The code and dataset will be publicly available.

rag_package.related_work_summary: Existing research in embodied intelligence primarily focuses on indoor scenarios, leading to limited task difficulty and a significant gap to artificial general intelligence (Gao et al., 2024; Xia et al., 2018). While some works attempt to build 3D urban environments for Embodied AI, such as MetaUrban (Wu et al., 2024), they often employ simplified environments or focus on fictional cities, thereby restricting the validation of embodied agents' capabilities. Efforts to improve navigation systems, even in indoor contexts, highlight the importance of spatial models and context awareness (Afyouni et al., 2012). The broader application of AI in smart cities (Yiitcanlar et al., 2020) and real-world robotics (Kawaharazuka et al., 2024) indicates a growing interest in integrating AI into complex environments. However, challenges persist in developing intelligent agents that can perceive, plan, and act effectively in dynamic, open-world settings, as underscored by future directions in Vision-and-Language Navigation (Gu et al., 2022) and the complexities of urban mobility (Alessandretti and Szell, 2022). This paper addresses these limitations by introducing "EmbodiedCity," a benchmark platform designed to extend embodied agents from indoor spaces to highly realistic, real-world city environments.

3.desc: No RAG, 2 iterations, 1 reviewer, AI Detector enabled, no author rebuttal

strengths: The paper introduces 'EmbodiedCity', a highly novel benchmark platform that moves Embodied AI beyond bounded indoor environments into realistic, open-world cityscapes based on real-world data. This is a significant leap forward.

The platform offers a comprehensive set of tasks covering perception, reasoning, and decision-making (scene understanding, QA, dialogue, VLN, task planning), which is crucial for advancing towards AGI in complex urban settings.

The commitment to an open platform, including executable programs, Python libraries, and an online service, greatly enhances the potential impact and accessibility of this research for the wider community.
weaknesses: The reliance on human refinement for ground truth data, especially for a dataset of 87.1k cases, raises questions about scalability and potential for subtle biases, even though it's acknowledged as a practical necessity.

The evaluation section, though informative, could benefit from more in-depth qualitative analysis of *why* certain models perform better on specific tasks, beyond general statements about model size or language understanding. For instance, what specific visual cues are smaller models missing that GPT-4 Turbo picks up in counting tasks?
reviewers.summary_comment: This paper presents a truly exciting and forward-looking contribution to the field of Embodied AI. The core idea of bringing embodied agents into realistic, open-world urban environments is highly novel and addresses a critical limitation of previous research. The construction of a high-fidelity 3D simulation environment based on a real city, coupled with a diverse set of benchmark tasks, has immense potential to push the boundaries of AI research towards Artificial General Intelligence. While there are inherent challenges in large-scale dataset creation and some minor details in the evaluations could be expanded, these do not overshadow the groundbreaking nature and significance of 'EmbodiedCity'. The potential for this platform to inspire future work and serve as a crucial tool for both pre-training and sim2real transfer is enormous. This work clearly pushes the field forward and deserves to be recognized.

why_it_fits: The paper introduces a novel benchmark platform for Embodied AI in real-world city environments, directly aligning with 'general machine learning' that advances core ML capabilities and 'application-driven machine learning' for innovative techniques and challenging problems relevant to practical scenarios.

The benchmark includes tasks covering perception, reasoning, and decision-making (e.g., scene understanding, QA, dialogue, VLN, task planning), which are central to various sub-fields of machine learning, including deep learning, reinforcement learning, and trustworthy machine learning (considering the complexity of real-world environments).

The development of a high-fidelity 3D simulation environment, complete with executable programs, Python libraries, and an online service, resonates with the 'machine learning systems' topic by offering improved implementation, scalability, and distributed methods for research.
The evaluation of popular large language models on this benchmark directly contributes to the understanding of their capabilities in embodied tasks, a crucial aspect for advancing AI research.

Reviewer A highlights the 'highly novel benchmark platform' and its 'significant leap forward' for Embodied AI, emphasizing that it 'pushes the boundaries of AI research towards Artificial General Intelligence', which are strong indicators of fit for a top-tier ML conference like ICML.
why_it_does_not_fit: While the paper is strong, its primary contribution is a benchmark platform and dataset, which might be less focused on novel algorithmic development or theoretical advancements compared to some other ICML submissions. However, benchmarks are explicitly welcome in application-driven ML.

The reviewer's concern about the 'reliance on human refinement for ground truth data raises questions about scalability and potential for subtle biases' and the desire for 'more in-depth qualitative analysis of *why* certain models perform better' indicates areas that, while not disqualifying, could be perceived as less rigorous compared to pure theoretical or algorithmic papers.

why_it_fits: The paper directly addresses emerging challenges in 'Robotics, embodied systems, and engineering' by providing a benchmark for embodied agents in complex, open-world city environments.

The various evaluation tasks, specifically 'Computer vision' (scene understanding), 'Language and multimodal language models' (QA, dialogue, VLN), 'Decision-making, reinforcement learning, and control' (task planning, navigation), and 'General machine learning' (core contributions in supervised and unsupervised methods as applied in the benchmark), align well with NeurIPS's interdisciplinary nature.
The emphasis on moving Embodied AI towards 'Artificial General Intelligence' aligns with NeurIPS's broad scope and interest in foundational AI challenges.

The creation of a high-quality 3D simulation environment based on real-world data and the provision of an open platform (SDK, online service) are valuable contributions that could attract researchers in data-centric AI and SysML Infrastructure, both listed NeurIPS topics.

Reviewer A praises the 'highly novel benchmark platform' and its 'significant leap forward', which is a type of impactful contribution NeurIPS welcomes, especially for fostering new research directions in embodied AI.
why_it_does_not_fit: Similar to ICML, the primary contribution is a benchmark and dataset, rather than a novel algorithm or theory. While NeurIPS does welcome such contributions, the emphasis might slightly lean towards algorithmic innovation.

The reviewer's comment about the need for 'more in-depth qualitative analysis' of model performance, beyond observing which models perform better, suggests that the analytical depth might need to be enhanced for some NeurIPS audiences who might seek deeper insights into model failures or successes.

The 'Others' topic category, while broad, might position the paper neutrally. However, the strong alignment with 'Robotics, embodied systems' specifically could help. The reviewer's positive assessment mitigates this concern.

why_it_fits: The evaluation of various large language models (LLMs) and multi-modal models (Fuyu-8B, Qwen-VL, Claude 3, GPT-4 Turbo) on embodied tasks is highly relevant to ICLR's strong focus on deep learning, representation learning, and generative models.

The tasks involve advanced aspects of deep learning, such as 'unsupervised, self-supervised, semi-supervised, and supervised representation learning' through scene understanding, and 'representation learning for computer vision, audio, language, and other modalities' within the urban context.
The introduction of a new benchmark and datasets for embodied agents in complex urban environments directly supports 'datasets and benchmarks' as a relevant topic for ICLR.
The potential for this platform to support 'applications to robotics, autonomy, planning' is explicitly mentioned in ICLR's topics of interest, as embodied AI is a key area for robotics.

Reviewer A acknowledges the 'groundbreaking nature and significance' of the platform in pushing Embodied AI forward, which ICLR values for advancing the state of the art in deep learning and related fields.
why_it_does_not_fit: While deep learning models are evaluated, the core contribution is the benchmark platform itself, rather than a novel deep learning architecture or significant theoretical advances in deep learning, which might be a higher priority for ICLR submissions.

The reviewer's concern about the 'reliance on human refinement for ground truth data' and the desire for more 'qualitative analysis' could be seen as a minor weakness in methodological rigor for a conference deeply focused on the technical nuances of deep learning models.
The 'Others' topic, combined with a focus on a platform rather than a DL model, might require careful positioning to emphasize its relevance to deep learning researchers at ICLR.

strengths: The paper introduces a highly novel and significant benchmark for embodied AI in real-world urban environments, moving beyond the traditional indoor or fictional settings. This is a crucial step towards AGI.

The development of a realistic 3D simulation environment based on a real city (Beijing) with detailed buildings, streets, vehicles, and pedestrians is an outstanding achievement, offering high fidelity and continuous sensing/motion capabilities.

The proposed benchmark includes a diverse and comprehensive set of five embodied tasks (scene understanding, QA, dialogue, VLN, task planning) that effectively cover perception, reasoning, and decision-making abilities, which are essential for embodied intelligence and push the boundaries of current evaluation paradigms.
weaknesses: The initial lack of concrete model-centric ideas or challenges within the main paper, beyond general LLM performance, was a weakness. While the authors' rebuttal promises to address this with specific examples, the current version still lacks these details.

The specific methodological details regarding the human refinement process, such as inter-annotator agreement and quantified efforts, were absent in the submission. The authors' commitment to include these in the supplementary materials for the camera-ready version is positive, but the lack of these details in the reviewed version remains a methodological gap.
reviewers.summary_comment: The authors have clearly understood and committed to addressing the weaknesses identified, and their proposed revisions are very satisfactory. The intention to include more concrete, model-centric challenges directly linked to the unique aspects of the urban environment is exactly what aforward-looking researcher hopes for in such a pioneering benchmark. Similarly, detailing the human refinement process with specific metrics like inter-annotator agreement and quantified effort will significantly bolster the methodological rigor and trustworthiness of the dataset. While these improvements are not present in the current version, the authors' proactive and detailed response instills confidence that the final paper will be substantially strengthened. Given the outstanding novelty and significance of 'EmbodiedCity' as a benchmark for real-world urban embodied AI, and the authors' clear commitment to refining the identified weaknesses, my decision to accept remains firm. This work is a crucial development for the field.

why_it_fits: The paper introduces a benchmark platform for Embodied AI, which falls under 'general machine learning' and 'application-driven machine learning', especially relevant given the focus on robotics and real-world interactions.

The development of a highly realistic 3D simulation environment and diverse embodied tasks aligns with ICML's interest in cutting-edge research and important application areas like robotics and machine vision.
The paper provides a new benchmark and dataset, which is a significant contribution to the machine learning community and aligns with ICML's focus on foundational advances.

The evaluation of popular large language models on this new benchmark provides empirical results relevant to ICML's deep learning track and highlights model capabilities in complex, real-world inspired settings.
why_it_does_not_fit: While Embodied AI is a relevant topic, the paper's primary contribution is a benchmark platform rather than a novel machine learning algorithm or theoretical advancement, which some ICML submissions heavily focus on. Reviewer A notes a 'lack of concrete model-centric ideas or challenges within the main paper'.

The methodological details regarding the human refinement process were initially absent, indicating a potential weakness in the rigor of the dataset creation as highlighted by Reviewer A, though the authors committed to addressing this.

why_it_fits: The topic of Embodied AI in real-world urban environments directly aligns with NeurIPS's stated topics, especially 'Robotics, embodied systems, and engineering', as well as 'Data-centric aspects of AI' and 'General machine learning: core contributions in supervised and unsupervised methods'.

The creation of a high-fidelity simulation environment and benchmark dataset for complex embodied tasks is a significant contribution that NeurIPS, as an interdisciplinary meeting, would value for advancing the field of AI and ML.

paper_metadata.title: ChatGPT Utility in Healthcare Education, Research, and Practice: Systematic Review on the Promising Perspectives and Valid Concerns
paper_metadata.abstract: ChatGPT is an artificial intelligence (AI)-based conversational large language model (LLM). The potential applications of LLMs in health care education, research, and practice could be promising if the associated valid concerns are proactively examined and addressed. The current systematic review aimed to investigate the utility of ChatGPT in health care education, research, and practice and to highlight its potential limitations. Using the PRIMSA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted to retrieve English records in PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar (published research or preprints) that examined ChatGPT in the context of health care education, research, or practice. A total of 60 records were eligible for inclusion. Benefits of ChatGPT were cited in 51/60 (85.0%) records and included: (1) improved scientific writing and enhancing research equity and versatility; (2) utility in health care research (efficient analysis of datasets, code generation, literature reviews, saving time to focus on experimental design, and drug discovery and development); (3) benefits in health care practice (streamlining the workflow, cost saving, documentation, personalized medicine, and improved health literacy); and (4) benefits in health care education including improved personalized learning and the focus on critical thinking and problem-based learning. Concerns regarding ChatGPT use were stated in 58/60 (96.7%) records including ethical, copyright, transparency, and legal issues, the risk of bias, plagiarism, lack of originality, inaccurate content with risk of hallucination, limited knowledge, incorrect citations, cybersecurity issues, and risk of infodemics. The promising applications of ChatGPT can induce paradigm shifts in health care education, research, and practice. However, the embrace of this AI chatbot should be conducted with extreme caution considering its potential limitations. As it currently stands, ChatGPT does not qualify to be listed as an author in scientific articles unless the ICMJE/COPE guidelines are revised or amended. An initiative involving all stakeholders in health care education, research, and practice is urgently needed. This will help to set a code of ethics to guide the responsible use of ChatGPT among other LLMs in health care and academia.

paper_metadata.title: Lexicon-Based Methods for Sentiment Analysis
paper_metadata.abstract: We present a lexicon-based approach to extracting sentiment from text. The Semantic Orientation CALculator (SO-CAL) uses dictionaries of words annotated with their semantic orientation (polarity and strength), and incorporates intensification and negation. SO-CAL is applied to the polarity classification task, the process of assigning a positive or negative label to a text that captures the text's opinion towards its main subject matter. We show that SO-CAL's performance is consistent across domains and in completely unseen data. Additionally, we describe the process of dictionary creation, and our use of Mechanical Turk to check dictionaries for consistency and reliability.

Facebook as a research tool for the social sciences: Opportunities, challenges, ethical considerations, and practical guidelines.
paper_metadata.abstract: Facebook is rapidly gaining recognition as a powerful research tool for the social sciences. It constitutes a large and diverse pool of participants, who can be selectively recruited for both online and offline studies. Additionally, it facilitates data collection by storing detailed records of its users' demographic profiles, social interactions, and behaviors. With participants' consent, these data can be recorded retrospectively in a convenient, accurate, and inexpensive way. Based on our experience in designing, implementing, and maintaining multiple Facebook-based psychological studies that attracted over 10 million participants, we demonstrate how to recruit participants using Facebook, incentivize them effectively, and maximize their engagement. We also outline the most important opportunities and challenges associated with using Facebook for research, provide several practical guidelines on how to successfully implement studies on Facebook, and finally, discuss ethical considerations.

paper_metadata.title: A survey on large language model based autonomous agents
paper_metadata.abstract: Abstract Autonomous agents have long been a research focus in academic and industry communities. Previous research often focuses on training agents with limited knowledge within isolated environments, which diverges significantly from human learning processes, and makes the agents hard to achieve human-like decisions. Recently, through the acquisition of vast amounts of Web knowledge, large language models (LLMs) have shown potential in human-level intelligence, leading to a surge in research on LLM-based autonomous agents. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of these studies, delivering a systematic review of LLM-based autonomous agents from a holistic perspective. We first discuss the construction of LLM-based autonomous agents, proposing a unified framework that encompasses much of previous work. Then, we present a overview of the diverse applications of LLM-based autonomous agents in social science, natural science, and engineering. Finally, we delve into the evaluation strategies commonly used for LLM-based autonomous agents. Based on the previous studies, we also present several challenges and future directions in this field.

paper_metadata.title: GPT is an effective tool for multilingual psychological text analysis
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
paper_metadata.abstract: The social and behavioral sciences have been increasingly using automated text analysis to measure psychological constructs in text. We explore whether GPT, the large-language model (LLM) underlying the AI chatbot ChatGPT, can be used as a tool for automated psychological text analysis in several languages. Across 15 datasets ( n = 47,925 manually annotated tweets and news headlines), we tested whether different versions of GPT (3.5 Turbo, 4, and 4 Turbo) can accurately detect psychological constructs (sentiment, discrete emotions, offensiveness, and moral foundations) across 12 languages. We found that GPT ( r = 0.59 to 0.77) performed much better than English-language dictionary analysis ( r = 0.20 to 0.30) at detecting psychological constructs as judged by manual annotators. GPT performed nearly as well as, and sometimes better than, several top-performing fine-tuned machine learning models. Moreover, GPT’s performance improved across successive versions of the model, particularly for lesser-spoken languages, and became less expensive. Overall, GPT may be superior to many existing methods of automated text analysis, since it achieves relatively high accuracy across many languages, requires no training data, and is easy to use with simple prompts (e.g., “is this text negative?”) and little coding experience. We provide sample code and a video tutorial for analyzing text with the GPT application programming interface. We argue that GPT and other LLMs help democratize automated text analysis by making advanced natural language processing capabilities more accessible, and may help facilitate more cross-linguistic research with understudied languages.

paper_metadata.title: Bias and Unfairness in Information Retrieval Systems: New Challenges in the LLM Era
paper_metadata.abstract: With the rapid advancements of large language models (LLMs), information retrieval (IR) systems, such as search engines and recommender systems, have undergone a significant paradigm shift. This evolution, while heralding new opportunities, introduces emerging challenges, particularly in terms of biases and unfairness, which may threaten the information ecosystem. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of existing works on emerging and pressing bias and unfairness issues in IR systems when the integration of LLMs. We first unify bias and unfairness issues as distribution mismatch problems, providing a groundwork for categorizing various mitigation strategies through distribution alignment. Subsequently, we systematically delve into the specific bias and unfairness issues arising from three critical stages of LLMs integration into IR systems: data collection, model development, and result evaluation. In doing so, we meticulously review and analyze recent literature, focusing on the definitions, characteristics, and corresponding mitigation strategies associated with these issues. Finally, we identify and highlight some open problems and challenges for future work, aiming to inspire researchers and stakeholders in the IR field and beyond to better understand and mitigate bias and unfairness issues of IR in this LLM era. We also consistently maintain a GitHub repository for the relevant papers and resources in this rising direction at https://github.com/KID-22/LLM-IR-Bias-Fairness-Survey.

paper_metadata.title: Perils and opportunities in using large language models in psychological research
paper_metadata.abstract: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has sparked considerable interest in their potential application in psychological research, mainly as a model of the human psyche or as a general text-analysis tool. However, the trend of using LLMs without sufficient attention to their limitations and risks, which we rhetorically refer to as "GPTology", can be detrimental given the easy access to models such as ChatGPT. Beyond existing general guidelines, we investigate the current limitations, ethical implications, and potential of LLMs specifically for psychological research, and show their concrete impact in various empirical studies. Our results highlight the importance of recognizing global psychological diversity, cautioning against treating LLMs (especially in zero-shot settings) as universal solutions for text analysis, and developing transparent, open methods to address LLMs' opaque nature for reliable, reproducible, and robust inference from AI-generated data. Acknowledging LLMs' utility for task automation, such as text annotation, or to expand our understanding of human psychology, we argue for diversifying human samples and expanding psychology's methodological toolbox to promote an inclusive, generalizable science, countering homogenization, and over-reliance on LLMs.

paper_metadata.title: What we really want to find by Sentiment Analysis: The Relationship between Computational Models and Psychological State
paper_metadata.abstract: As the first step to model emotional state of a person, we build sentiment analysis models with existing deep neural network algorithms and compare the models with psychological measurements to enlighten the relationship. In the experiments, we first examined psychological state of 64 participants and asked them to summarize the story of a book, Chronicle of a Death Foretold (Marquez, 1981). Secondly, we trained models using crawled 365,802 movie review data; then we evaluated participants' summaries using the pretrained model as a concept of transfer learning. With the background that emotion affects on memories, we investigated the relationship between the evaluation score of the summaries from computational models and the examined psychological measurements. The result shows that although CNN performed the best among other deep neural network algorithms (LSTM, GRU), its results are not related to the psychological state. Rather, GRU shows more explainable results depending on the psychological state. The contribution of this paper can be summarized as follows: (1) we enlighten the relationship between computational models and psychological measurements. (2) we suggest this framework as objective methods to evaluate the emotion; the real sentiment analysis of a person.

paper_metadata.title: SemEval-2015 Task 10: Sentiment Analysis in Twitter
paper_metadata.abstract: In this paper, we describe the 2015 iteration of the SemEval shared task on Sentiment Analysis in Twitter. This was the most popular sentiment analysis shared task to date with more than 40 teams participating in each of the last three years. This year's shared task competition consisted of five sentiment prediction subtasks. Two were reruns from previous years: (A) sentiment expressed by a phrase in the context of a tweet, and (B) overall sentiment of a tweet. We further included three new subtasks asking to predict (C) the sentiment towards a topic in a single tweet, (D) the overall sentiment towards a topic in a set of tweets, and (E) the degree of prior polarity of a phrase.

rag_package.related_work_summary: Evaluating psychological traits in Large Language Models (LLMs) requires robust methods to ensure reliability and validity. Building upon foundational work in construct validity for psychological tests (Cronbach and Meehl, 1955), recent research has begun to explore the capabilities of LLMs in this domain. For instance, (Rathje et al., 2024) demonstrate GPT's effectiveness for multilingual psychological text analysis, providing a strong baseline for assessing LLM performance in detecting psychological constructs. However, the application of LLMs in psychological research also presents significant perils and opportunities, demanding careful consideration of limitations and ethical implications for reliable inference (Abdurahman et al., 2024). The relationship between computational models and psychological states, particularly in sentiment analysis, has been a long-standing area of inquiry (Jo et al., 2017), with methods ranging from lexicon-based approaches (Taboada et al., 2011) to more complex evaluations within shared tasks (Rosenthal et al., 2019). Current surveys on LLM-based autonomous agents also highlight the evolving evaluation strategies necessary for these systems (Wang et al., 2024). Furthermore, discussions on the challenges of LLMs often include ethical aspects, such as those in educational contexts (Kasneci et al., 2023) and the emergence of bias and unfairness in LLM-driven systems (Dai et al., 2024), underscoring the critical need for enhanced reliability and validity in LLM psychological trait evaluation.

3.desc: No RAG, 2 iterations, 1 reviewer, AI Detector enabled, no author rebuttal

strengths: The core idea of adapting the Implicit Association Test (IAT) for LLMs to measure implicit sentiment is highly novel and creative, moving beyond simplistic self-reported psychometric evaluations. This bottom-up approach is exactly the kind of innovative thinking the field needs.

The paper addresses a significant and acknowledged limitation in current LLM evaluation: the unreliability and invalidity of human-derived psychometric tests when applied to AI. This work offers a robust and practical solution to a pressing problem.

The extensive scope of the CSI with 5,000 carefully selected neutral words, covering both English and Chinese, represents a substantial effort and significantly broadens the assessment capabilities compared to traditional methods. The qualitative analysis it enables is also valuable.
weaknesses: While the concept is robust, the selection of "comedy" and "tragedy" as the primary antithetical terms might be too simplistic for capturing the full spectrum of implicit sentiment. The ablation study in Appendix C.3 hints at this, showing that stronger terms ("good"/"bad") significantly affect scores and reluctance. A deeper theoretical justification for these specific terms, or a broader exploration of semantic dimensions, would strengthen the approach.

The evaluation of predictive power (RQ3) relies on one specific task (story generation) and subsequent sentiment scoring by another LLM (Qwen2-72B-Instruct). While a good start, the robustness of this "predictive power" would benefit from validation against a wider range of downstream tasks and potentially human-evaluated sentiment, to fully convince that CSI scores indeed predict real-world model behavior across various applications.
reviewers.summary_comment: This paper presents a truly innovative and conceptually strong approach to evaluating LLMs' underlying emotional and psychological traits. The adoption of the Implicit Association Test (IAT) to create the Core Sentiment Inventory (CSI) is a bold move that directly tackles the well-documented reliability and validity issues of traditional psychometric scales when applied to AI. The idea of using a broad, implicitly neutral word set to uncover latent sentiment tendencies is particularly exciting, offering a more authentic representation of an LLM's internal associations. While there are minor concerns about the chosen semantic axis ('comedy'/'tragedy') and the breadth of predictive validity evaluation, these are overshadowed by the strong novelty and significant potential impact of this work. The paper is well-written and the experimental results convincingly demonstrate improved reliability and a promising degree of predictive power. This is a clear step forward in responsible AI development and understanding the complex characteristics of LLMs. It opens up many avenues for future research.

why_it_fits: The paper introduces a novel evaluation methodology (CSI) for LLMs, which aligns well with ICML's interest in 'general machine learning' and 'trustworthy machine learning' (reliability, interpretability, safety). The focus on systematic evaluation and understanding LLM characteristics is highly relevant.

The 'contribution fit' is strong, as the paper proposes a new method (CSI) inspired by a well-established psychological test (IAT) adapted for LLMs, demonstrating both theoretical innovation in evaluation and empirical validation with state-of-the-art models. This blend of methodological advancement and empirical results is highly valued.

Reviewer A explicitly notes the 'highly novel and creative' adaptation of IAT for LLMs and that it addresses a 'significant and acknowledged limitation in current LLM evaluation,' indicating a strong 'novelty fit' for ICML, which emphasizes cutting-edge research.

The paper provides rigorous experimental testing of the CSI method, comparing its reliability and validity against traditional BFI methods, with clear quantitative improvements (e.g., consistency rate, reluctancy rate). This scientific rigor is expected at ICML.
The paper is well-written and clearly positions its contribution, as highlighted by Reviewer A, making it suitable for presentation at a top-tier conference like ICML.

The use of bilingual evaluation (English and Chinese) and the careful construction of the word set (5,000 neutral words) demonstrate a comprehensive approach to an important problem, fitting ICML's broad scope.
why_it_does_not_fit: Reviewer A points out that the choice of 'comedy'/'tragedy' as primary antithetical terms might be too simplistic and suggests 'a deeper theoretical justification or a broader exploration of semantic dimensions.' While not a disqualifier, this indicates a potential area for further theoretical grounding which is often a strength of ICML papers.

The 'evaluation of predictive power relies on one specific task (story generation)', which Reviewer A suggests could be expanded to 'a wider range of downstream tasks and potentially human-evaluated sentiment.' This limitation in the breadth of empirical validation could be perceived as a minor weakness in terms of comprehensive evaluation, a core aspect of ICML research.

why_it_fits: The paper's focus on understanding 'inherent characteristics, such as personalities, temperaments, and emotions' of LLMs falls under NeurIPS's broad interest in 'General machine learning: core contributions in supervised and unsupervised methods' and 'Socio-technical aspects of AI' and 'Human interaction in AI systems', particularly concerning responsible AI development.

The reliance on 'one specific task (story generation)' for validity assessment, as noted by Reviewer A, might be a slightly weaker 'evaluation fit' for NeurIPS which often expects broad and robust validation for significant methodological contributions, especially given its interdisciplinary nature often requires demonstrating utility across various domains.

strengths: The core idea of adapting the Implicit Association Test (IAT) to evaluate LLM sentiment implicitly is highly novel and a significant departure from traditional psychometric methods, which are clearly failing for LLMs.

The paper addresses a critical, forward-looking concern in AI development: understanding the inherent psychological characteristics of LLMs beyond task performance. The proposed method directly tackles the limitations of model reluctance and inconsistency seen in previous approaches.

The demonstration of increased reliability and predictive power, especially in cross-language contexts and real-world tasks like story generation, makes a strong case for CSI's utility and potential impact.
weaknesses: The additional statistical analysis regarding the reliability claims, while promised, is still not integrated into the current version of the paper. This integration is crucial for fully substantiating the claims of improved reliability.

The 'neutral score' calculation, which conflates inconsistent responses with explicitly neutral ones, presents a potential area for more granular analysis in future work, as acknowledged by the authors.
reviewers.summary_comment: This paper offers a highly novel and significant contribution by introducing the Core Sentiment Inventory (CSI) for implicitly evaluating the sentiment tendencies of Large Language Models. The creative adaptation of the Implicit Association Test (IAT) provides a much-needed alternative to traditional psychometric methods, which are ill-suited for LLMs. The paper effectively demonstrates CSI's improved reliability and predictive power across different languages and practical tasks like story generation. The authors have consistently acknowledged the need to integrate detailed statistical analysis for their reliability claims, which, once implemented in the final version, will further solidify the paper's empirical backing. The acknowledged nuance in the 'neutral score' calculation, while a minor point, is a good indicator of self-awareness. Overall, the work is ambitious, forward-looking, and holds substantial promise for advancing responsible AI development. It is an excellent example of bold research that should be accepted.

strengths: The core idea of adapting the Implicit Association Test (IAT) for LLMs to measure implicit sentiment is highly novel and creative, moving beyond the limitations of human-centric psychometric scales.

The paper states that the choice of 'comedy'/'tragedy' for the IAT prompt is guided by two principles; however, a more thorough justification or ablation study on *why* these two specific words are superior to other mild contrasting pairs would further strengthen the argument.
reviewers.summary_comment: This paper presents a truly innovative approach to evaluating the psychological traits, specifically sentiment tendencies, of Large Language Models. Moving away from human-derived questionnaires towards an implicit, bottom-up method inspired by the IAT is a bold and much-needed step forward. The proposed Core Sentiment Inventory (CSI) addresses critical issues like model reluctance and inconsistency that plague current evaluation methods. The significant improvements in reliability and the demonstration of predictive validity in a practical task like story generation are compelling. While there might be minor aspects of the methodology that could be further refined (e.g., deeper exploration of the chosen sentiment descriptors), the core idea and its potential to unlock more robust and nuanced understanding of LLM 'psychology' make this a highly significant contribution. This work has the potential to inspire a new generation of LLM evaluation frameworks, aligning perfectly with my preference for novel and impactful research. The minor imperfections do not undermine the overall innovativeness and importance of the proposed method.

strengths: The paper rigorously addresses significant methodological limitations of current psychometric evaluations for LLMs, specifically 'model reluctance' and 'poor consistency', by proposing a novel, implicit approach.

The methodology for constructing the Core Sentiment Inventory (CSI) is well-defined, emphasizing the selection of neutral nouns and verbs and utilizing a broad, data-driven set of common words to ensure representativeness and minimize bias.

The evaluation includes a comprehensive set of experiments comparing CSI to traditional methods (BFI) across reliability (consistency and reluctance rates) and validity (predictive power in story generation), showcasing clear superiority of CSI.
weaknesses: While the paper adopts the IAT framework, the interpretation of 'comedy' and 'tragedy' as sentiment dimensions could be further elaborated, especially when considering the nuances of human emotion captured by these terms versus a simple positive/negative dichotomy. The connection between 'comedy'/'tragedy' and 'optimism'/'pessimism' could benefit from deeper theoretical justification.

The prompt used for story generation ('Please write a story using the following words') is quite open-ended. While the sentiment of generated stories is evaluated by another LLM, the direct link between input word sentiment ratio and the LLM's 'inherent' sentiment, as opposed to its ability to follow instructions, could be scrutinized more deeply. It is an indirect measure of 'validity'.
reviewers.summary_comment: This paper presents a strong case for Core Sentiment Inventory (CSI) as a more robust and reliable method for evaluating the sentiment tendencies of Large Language Models. It meticulously outlines the deficiencies of existing human-derived psychometric tests when applied to LLMs and proposes a well-justified alternative based on the Implicit Association Test. The methodology for constructing CSI, focusing on neutral words and vast item sets, is sound. The experimental evaluation is comprehensive, demonstrating significant improvements in reliability and predictive power compared to traditional methods. The ablation studies further reinforce the robustness of CSI. While the interpretation of 'comedy' and 'tragedy' as direct sentiment proxies could be somewhat nuanced, and the validity assessment relies on a cascaded LLM evaluation, the overall contributions to methodological rigor in LLM psychometric evaluation are substantial. The paper is clearly written and the results are well-presented.

strengths: The paper successfully identifies and addresses a critical practical limitation of current LLM psychometric evaluations: poor reliability and validity due to model reluctance and inconsistency when using human-centric assessments. The proposed CSI method offers a tangible improvement.

The Core Sentiment Inventory (CSI) is well-designed and practically relevant. Its inspiration from IAT, use of a broad range of neutral words, and bilingual coverage make it a robust and comprehensive tool for practitioners wanting to understand LLM sentiment tendencies.

The experimental evaluation is thorough, demonstrating clear improvements in reliability (consistency rate, reluctance rate) and establishing predictive validity through the story generation task. The ablation studies further strengthen the findings by showing robustness to parameter changes and highlighting the importance of word selection.
weaknesses: While the concept of 'optimism,' 'pessimism,' and 'neutrality' is used, linking these directly to complex human psychological concepts like 'personality' or 'temperament' in LLMs could be more carefully nuanced. The paper's conclusion regarding 'emotional alignment' or 'psychological traits' might overstate the current scope of what CSI measures, which is primarily sentiment association.

The prompt structure for the CSI (e.g., "comedy" or "tragedy") could be further explored for potential biases or alternative phrasing that might yield different implicit associations. The ablation study touched on this with 'good/bad' but a deeper analysis of the target sentiment words themselves could be valuable.
reviewers.summary_comment: This paper presents a strong practical contribution to the field of LLM evaluation by introducing the Core Sentiment Inventory (CSI). It tackles a significant problem with existing psychometric evaluations, which often suffer from poor reliability and validity when applied to LLMs. The CSI, inspired by the Implicit Association Test, offers a more robust and less susceptible method for assessing sentiment tendencies. The work is clearly presented, and the experimental results convincingly demonstrate that CSI improves consistency, reduces model reluctance, and holds predictive power for LLM behavior in generative tasks. The focus on practical impact and real-world applicability makes this a valuable paper for researchers and practitioners alike. While the interpretation of 'psychological traits' warrants a bit more humility, the core contribution of a more reliable sentiment evaluation tool is significant.

target_paper_summary.title: Recovering Plasticity Of Neural Networks Via Soft Weight Rescaling
target_paper_summary.abstract: Recent studies have shown that as training progresses, neural networks gradually lose their capacity to learn new information, a phenomenon known as plasticity loss. An unbounded weight growth is one of the main causes of plasticity loss. Furthermore, it harms generalization capability and disrupts optimization dynamics. Re-initializing the network can be a solution, but it results in the loss of learned information, leading to performance drops. In this paper, we propose Soft Weight Rescaling (SWR), a novel approach that prevents unbounded weight growth without losing information. SWR recovers the plasticity of the network by simply scaling down the weight at each step of the learning process. We theoretically prove that SWR bounds weight magnitude and balances weight magnitude between layers. Our experiment shows that SWR improves performance on warm-start learning, continual learning, and single-task learning setups on standard image classification benchmarks.
